::: {.callout-warning}
## Target flow, not an installed-version guarantee
The figures show the approved lifecycle direction, with implementation status marked
explicitly. **The installed `0.4.0-preview.1` does not implement this complete
flow.** In particular, the new settings layout and clear/hook ordering still need
reviewed, merged code and event-order tests. PR159 implements a draft of this order;
it is not a new release or completion of all defaults, R-data and embedding work.
Use sample data or a disposable project copy.
Previews are not a security sandbox.
:::

## Read the figures

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[R] Released** | Bounded behavior in [0.4.0-preview.1](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.4.0-preview.1), not a complete safety guarantee. |
| **[M] Main only** | A merged capability after that release; it is not automatically present in an installed binary. |
| **[D] Draft** | Implemented on the pinned PR159 review branch; not merged or released at this evidence point. |
| **[T] Target** | An approved requirement or integration step awaiting matching implementation/tests. |
| **[?] Open** | A proposal or placement decision still requiring confirmation. |

A capability marked **[R]** or **[M]** inside a target figure does **not** prove
that all surrounding arrows are implemented. Solid arrows show the order being
specified. Dotted connections mark an unresolved association, not an execution step.

An **output build** means the production `proj build` path. A **preview** means
`proj build-dev`. Clearing here means final-output clearing, not arbitrary
deletion of project files or preparation of a fresh cache.

## The three stages

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-overview
%%| fig-cap: "Target overview. Open the stage details below for conditions and failure boundaries."
%%| fig-alt: "Three stages: verify setup and run start hooks; clear immediately around analysis when selected; finish a preview or output build with the stated limits."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  subgraph PRE["1 · Pre-build"]
    A["Resolve and verify basic setup"]
    B["[T] Start hooks, then remaining<br/>preparation"]
    A --> B
  end
  subgraph BUILD["2 · Build"]
    C["[T] Conditional pre-clear →<br/>ordered analysis → conditional<br/>post-clear"]
  end
  subgraph POST["3 · Post-build"]
    D["[T] Preview: end hooks and<br/>captured-state restoration; no<br/>publication"]
    E["[T/D] Output: promotion and<br/>enabled finalization; end hooks<br/>immediately before next-dev<br/>transition"]
  end
  B --> C
  C -->|"Preview"| D
  C -->|"Output"| E
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,B,C,D,E target
  style PRE fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
  style BUILD fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
  style POST fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
```

The key adjacency rules are deliberate: **nothing runs between pre-clear and
analysis**, or between **successful analysis and post-clear**. Start hooks come
after verified basic setup; end hooks come at the end, immediately before the
output build's transition to the next development version.

### 1. Pre-build details

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Open: resolution, validation, context and start hooks

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-pre
%%| fig-cap: "Target pre-build order. Existing capabilities are identified separately from new ordering."
%%| fig-alt: "Select root and profiles, validate merged configuration, capture run inputs, preflight targets and dependencies, capture recovery state, run start hooks, then finish preparation."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R] Select explicit or discovered<br/>project root"]
  B["[M/T] Resolve profiles and<br/>environment; merge config;<br/>settings HOW / build WHAT"]
  C["[R/T] Validate typed configuration<br/>and explicit resource mappings"]
  D["[M] Capture root, profiles,<br/>mappings, mode and active run<br/>version"]
  E["[R/T] Preflight selected inputs,<br/>targets, dependencies and enabled<br/>Git prerequisites"]
  F["[R] Capture bounded managed<br/>recovery state before controlled<br/>writes"]
  G["[T] Run configured start hooks"]
  H["[T] Complete remaining safe<br/>staging, renderer and allowed<br/>metadata preparation"]
  A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F --> G --> H
  classDef existing fill:#e5f2ed,stroke:#146859,color:#153b32
  classDef main fill:#e7effa,stroke:#315b89,color:#183954
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,F existing
  class D main
  class B,C,E,G,H target
```

- Root selection, effective profiles, merged configuration and environment must
  agree before analysis starts. The target assigns **HOW** choices to
  `settings` and **WHAT** is selected/run to `build`; this is not permission
  to add unknown fields to the installed preview.
- The captured context fixes resource identity and the active run version.
  At the pinned main baseline, preview retains an existing dev version or uses dev1 of a
  release without writing VERSION; an output run uses its requested release
  version throughout the run and leaves the subsequent dev1 only on success.
- Validate declared paths, selected script/hook inputs, supported renderer plans,
  dependencies and explicitly enabled Git actions before controlled build writes.
  Probes can have their own effects: this is not a blanket read-only/environment
  sanitization guarantee.
- Start/end refer to the existing pre/both and post/both hook sets, not new
  hook types. The requested change is their position in the lifecycle.
- Recovery capture must precede hooks and managed mutations. Cache/staging setup,
  supported renderer preparation and permitted metadata/ignore work finish before
  the final pre-clear gate. No new metadata/provenance record is implied here.
- A script's working directory is separate from project identity. Native cwd with
  an explicit project override, safe resource targets and render-context path
  presentation merged after the release in PR154–156; the evidence section
  separates those merges from the later lifecycle integration draft.

:::

### 2. Build details

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Open: exact clearing position and selected execution

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-build
%%| fig-cap: "Target clearing adjacency. The diamond checks select a branch; they are not extra lifecycle work."
%%| fig-alt: "With no analysis, skip execution and clearing. Otherwise an output pre-clear goes directly into ordered execution; successful execution goes directly to output post-clear if selected. Errors use recovery."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A{"Analysis selected?"}
  B{"Output build, promotion enabled<br/>and clear stage pre?"}
  C["[T] Pre-clear final outputs"]
  D["[T] Execute ordered scripts /<br/>supported renderer plan"]
  E{"Output build, promotion enabled<br/>and clear stage post?"}
  F["[T] Post-clear final outputs"]
  G["Continue to post-build"]
  N["[R/T] No analysis: skip renderer<br/>setup, analysis cleanup and<br/>execution"]
  X["Failure branch: stop success-only<br/>work and use bounded recovery"]
  A -->|"Yes"| B
  A -->|"Explicit empty list"| N --> G
  B -->|"Yes"| C --> D
  B -->|"No"| D
  D -->|"Success"| E
  D -->|"Failure"| X
  E -->|"Yes"| F --> G
  E -->|"No"| G
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class C,D,F,N target
```

Preview skips both final-output clear operations, even if an output setting asks
for them. With `scripts: []`, hooks can still run and an output build may export
existing artifacts; that is not proof of complete analysis-free retry identity.

The target routes eligible safe output/data roles and rendered docs through an
explicitly selected versioned cache, keeping configured final destinations
separate. Inputs retain their declared meaning; no undeclared `docs` or cache
mapping is invented. Ordinary scripts can still write elsewhere: path helpers and
staging are **not automatic isolation of every write**.

The selected execution order must follow the supported plan. Do not infer
arbitrary mixed-renderer ordering or RStudio/Quarto R API parity from this figure.

:::

### 3. Post-build details

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Open: promotion, end hooks, version and optional publication

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-post
%%| fig-cap: "Approved post-build order implemented in the pinned PR159 draft; not released."
%%| fig-alt: "Restore renderer configuration, stage and validate cache artifacts, restore native artifacts, then conditionally promote output. Enabled publication keeps a local release boundary, exports CAS and commits or pushes Git before end hooks and the next-development bump. Previews skip promotion and publication."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[T/D] Restore renderer config;<br/>stage and validate cache artifacts;<br/>restore native artifacts"]
  B{"Output build?"}
  C{"Analysis and promotion enabled?"}
  P["[T/D] Promote safe output/docs to<br/>explicitly configured final roots"]
  J{"Publication enabled?"}
  V["[D] Keep successful local release;<br/>close managed recovery boundary"]
  S["[D] Export configured local CAS<br/>destinations, if selected"]
  K["[D] Enabled Git commit / push"]
  D["[T/D] Run configured end hooks"]
  E{"Output build?"}
  F["[T/D] Transition to next<br/>development version"]
  G["[R/D] Restore captured managed<br/>state; retain cache results;<br/>no VERSION publication"]
  A --> B
  B -->|"Yes"| C
  C -->|"Yes"| P --> J
  C -->|"No: including empty analysis"| J
  J -->|"Yes"| V --> S --> K --> D
  J -->|"No"| D
  B -->|"Preview: skip promotion/publication"| D
  D --> E
  E -->|"Yes: immediately after end hooks"| F
  E -->|"Preview: no version transition"| G
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,P,V,S,K,D,F,G target
```

The end-hook/next-dev adjacency is approved. The pinned PR159 draft places
enabled CAS export and Git commit/push **before** end hooks and the next-dev
bump. Before publication it records the successful local release and gives up
the managed recovery snapshot. Publication or later end-hook failure preserves
that local release and skips the bump; partial external effects are not undone.
Without publication, end-hook failure still uses bounded managed recovery.
Preview runs end hooks, then restores captured managed state without a version
transition. These are draft implementation boundaries, not a released guarantee.

Promotion is output-only and conditional on selected analysis and enabled
promotion. Explicit empty analysis preserves existing upload inputs instead;
configured publication may still use them. Metadata means existing project/version operations,
not finished attempt/release identifiers or complete provenance. The implemented
storage path is configured local CAS export; Git commit/push and network checks
are opt-in, not consequences of merely having a Git repository.

An analysis failure does not enter the success-only post-clear/promotion/end-hook/version
path. This page does not introduce an always/finally-hook policy.

:::

## Settings being specified

| Choice | Target meaning and status |
|---|---|
| `settings.output-clear-stage` | **[T/D]** `none`, `pre` or `post`; default `none`. This canonical field is not available in installed 0.4.0-preview.1. |
| `pre` | **[T]** Clear immediately before selected analysis, after hooks and all other preparation. Output builds only. |
| `post` | **[T]** Clear immediately after successful analysis, before restoration, promotion, hooks or other finalization. Output builds only. |
| Resolution precedence | **[D] Pinned resolver:** explicit choice → merged `settings` YAML → legacy YAML → environment → default. This is PR159 source/test evidence; do not assume the installed preview exposes the new command/config choices. |
| Legacy compatibility | **[T/D]** Retain a compatibility path for `PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT` and `never`; map the old no-clear intent to canonical `none`. Do not assume mixed old/new settings are already accepted. |

At the pinned main baseline, the implementation reads the legacy environment ahead of the legacy YAML
`build.clear_output` value. It performs pre-cleanup before start hooks and
requested post-clear after local completion/export. Those are evidence of the
older implementation, **not** the newly approved ordering or the PR159 draft. See the pinned
baseline below rather than copying the target setting into an older binary.

## Failure and recovery boundaries

The local recovery figure describes the bounded captured-state rule. The separate
publication figure adds the **PR159 draft** boundary; it is not a whole-project
or remote rollback guarantee.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-local-failure
%%| fig-cap: "Existing local failure boundary: recovery covers only captured state."
%%| fig-alt: "Before recovery capture, rejection stops controlled build writes. After capture, local failures attempt bounded restoration and report restoration errors separately."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R/D] Preflight or managed local<br/>step fails; draft also covers end<br/>hooks when publication is off"]
  B{"Recovery capture exists?"}
  N["Stop: controlled build writes have<br/>not started"]
  C["Restore captured managed set"]
  D{"Restoration succeeds?"}
  E["Report local failure; permitted<br/>cache residue may remain"]
  F["Report primary and restoration<br/>errors; retain recovery data when<br/>available"]
  A --> B
  B -->|"No"| N
  B -->|"Yes"| C --> D
  D -->|"Yes"| E
  D -->|"No"| F
  classDef existing fill:#e5f2ed,stroke:#146859,color:#153b32
  class A,B,N,C,D,E,F existing
```

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-publication-failure
%%| fig-cap: "PR159 draft publication boundary: preserve local release; do not undo external effects."
%%| fig-alt: "After local success, establish the release boundary, then enabled CAS and Git publication, end hooks and next-development bump. A publication or end-hook failure preserves the release and skips the bump."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  G["[D] Local success; keep release<br/>version; close managed recovery"]
  H["[D] Enabled CAS export,<br/>then enabled Git commit / push"]
  J["[D] End hooks"]
  K["[D] Next-development bump"]
  I["[D] Publication/end-hook failure:<br/>preserve local release; skip bump;<br/>partial external effects remain"]
  G --> H
  H -->|"Success"| J -->|"Success"| K
  H -->|"Failure"| I
  J -->|"Failure"| I
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class G,H,J,K,I target
```

The captured managed set is not a whole-project or filesystem snapshot. Cache
results are deliberately retained. Arbitrary external script effects, concurrent
writers, crashes and partial storage/Git effects are outside a transactional
rollback guarantee. A preview restores its captured managed state on success
and failure; this does not make it a security sandbox.

Durable attempt/release records, complete input/code/config/dependency provenance
and safe analysis-free publication retries remain unfinished. Do not automatically
rerun analysis or claim publication was undone after an external failure.

## Evidence and version boundary

- **Installed preview:** [0.4.0-preview.1 source `bbd12ed`](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/tree/bbd12edc8de9865a96b6145d0c7702f1300cb1a8),
  [delivery evidence](release-delivery.qmd) and [preview limits](preview-status.qmd).
- **Main baseline for current-order statements:**
  [`c085632` build pipeline](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/blob/c085632bc31c0eac63e7b0ab03232be9b091ce84/src/build.rs).
  [PR153](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/153) adds captured run inputs
  after the release; it does not settle the new settings/clearing/hook order.
- **Merged after the preview release:** [safe logical targets, PR154](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/154),
  [path presentation, PR155](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/155) and
  [native cwd/override, PR156](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/156).
  These merges do not establish a new released binary or complete integration.
- **Implemented review draft:** [PR159 source `3459bad`](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/blob/3459badb7a1481ec81c5804ec51d87c23169fe4e/src/build.rs),
  [settings resolver at the same revision](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/blob/3459badb7a1481ec81c5804ec51d87c23169fe4e/src/yml.rs)
  and [executed remote renderer acceptance](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39576119854).
  This pins the clearing/hook/publication sequence and cache-consumer work under
  review. Defaults, R-data and embedding acceptance remain separate unfinished
  slices; this page does not mark them or M1/M2 complete.
- The [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) and [versioned compatibility log](compatibility.qmd)
  distinguish decisions, implementation and executed evidence. The
  [current implementation notes](flow.qmd) remain a separate view.

## Maintaining this figure

**Contributor requirement:** lifecycle changes must update this page's diagrams,
status legend and evidence/version references in the same PR. This includes
settings precedence, hook/clearing order, context/version capture, output
promotion and publication/failure boundaries. Link actual event-order and
recovery tests; do not turn a target marker into a released marker merely because
a branch compiles.

Keep the three-stage overview small. Put new detail in the relevant folded stage
instead of expanding one unreadable graph. Render the site, exercise diagram export and verify
the page links remotely; do not require local Quarto/R/Docker builds.
